topic: MBBS holders: can I practise in Germany?
details: Not automatically. You need recognition of your medical degree and a license (Approbation) from the state authority. Typical steps: documents recognition, German language B2 then medical language exam (Fachsprachprufung), and possibly a knowledge exam (Kenntnisprufung). Takes 1-2+ years; rules vary by state. Verify with the state authority.

topic: Can I study Medicine (MD) in Germany from India?
details: Medicine in Germany is taught in German, is state-regulated and extremely competitive. It is usually not a realistic path for most Indian students; many choose biomedical, public health or other health sciences Masters.
English-taught programs exist (for example in molecular medicine, neuroscience, biomedical engineering). Need relevant bachelor, good grades, IELTS 6.5; research experience helps.
English MPH programs exist (for example in Berlin and Heidelberg). Suitable for healthcare graduates, doctors, nurses, pharmacists; work experience often preferred.
Three-year vocational training in German hospitals/care; paid training; needs German (usually B1-B2). Programs such as Triple Win recruit nurses; verify current rules and costs.
To practise as a pharmacist you need a German license (Approbation) route; B.Pharm holders can also do MSc Pharmaceutical Sciences/Technology or pharma industry roles. Verify with authorities.
